newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast spot power climbs amid cold weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast spot power climbs amid cold weather.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the southeastern U.S. ended mostly higher Tuesday due to space-heating demand amid cold weather in much of the region.
Most of the Southeast was forecast on Wednesday to experience peak temperatures in the 30s-50s Fahrenheit and off-peak temperatures in the teens to 30s.
The Florida pennisula's temperatures were expected Wednesday to peak in the 60s-70s and to bottom in 30s-50s.

Peak, firm power for Wednesday delivery into the northwestern portion of Tennessee Valley Authority's (TVA) territory were valued at $29.00-$30.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), higher than Monday's highest deals done near $27.00.
In addition to higher demand, unscheduled plant outages in control areas north of TVA territory reduced the amount of power available to import into TVA.
Firm, next-day power for delivery into northwestern TVA during Wednesday's light load hours was pegged at $15.00-$16.00, down from Monday's quote near $18.00.
"There's plenty of off-peak power," a Florida trader said.
At the Georgia/Florida border, firm, peak electricity prices for Wednesday was mostly discussed at $31.00-$34.00, up sharply from Monday's range of $25.00-$29.00.
Firm, off-peak at the Ga./Fla. border for next-day delivery again stayed steady at $16.00-$18.00.
A 620 megawatt (MW) unit at the coal-fired Seminole generating station in Palatka, Fla., was planned to resume operation Wednesday following a seasonal maintenance outage.
The cold weather system was predicted to linger in the Southeast for the remainder of the week.
"They would stay the same," said a Houston trader, referring to spot power prices in the Southeast.
